name: Operational Excellence (OPS)
description: Operate, monitor, and continuously improve Couchbase cluster operations to deliver business value and mitigate risks.

questions.title: How do you monitor Couchbase health and establish actionable observability?
questions.description: Define baseline observability, core system metrics, and operational alerting to proactively detect degradation.

options.label: Monitor Bucket Resident Ratio, KV ops/sec, and latencies

risks.reason: No visibility on resident ratios or core service metrics can lead to silent degradation and heavy disk thrashing.

improvements.title: Implement Couchbase service-level monitoring
improvements.description: Track active resident ratios, KV throughput, and service-specific latencies to identify resource exhaustion early.

options.label: Use centralized telemetry and metrics endpoints

risks.reason: Fragmented or isolated cluster statistics slow down cross-tier incident root-cause analysis.

improvements.title: Centralize Couchbase telemetry
improvements.description: Integrate standard Couchbase Prometheus metric endpoints or Capella streaming integrations into unified platforms like Datadog or Grafana.

options.label: Enable completed requests logging for slow queries

risks.reason: Unindexed or heavy unoptimized SQL++ queries run undetected, consuming shared cluster CPU resources.

improvements.title: Capture and analyze slow SQL++ queries
improvements.description: Leverage the system:completed_requests catalog or log thresholds to audit and optimize slow query executions regularly.

options.label: Automate operational alerting with defined thresholds

risks.reason: Critical platform exceptions like auto-failover triggers or rebalance failures risk long recovery delays without automated notifications.

improvements.title: Configure infrastructure alerting thresholds
improvements.description: Set active alerts for node down events, unhealthily low bucket memory headroom, metadata chronicle status, and failed rebalances.

questions.title: How do you safely manage cluster topology changes and scaling events?
questions.description: Control platform risk during scaling, topology alterations, and failover events to maintain stable operations.

options.label: Execute controlled rebalances during scheduled windows

risks.reason: Triggering full rebalances under peak operational traffic shifts significant network and disk strain onto surviving nodes.

improvements.title: Establish predictable rebalance windows
improvements.description: Schedule capacity scaling tasks during off-peak windows to minimize the impact on active customer workloads.

options.label: Utilize Delta Node Recovery for transient node failures

risks.reason: Forcing full data re-syncs for nodes that were only offline briefly dramatically increases cluster recovery time and network overhead.

improvements.title: Prioritize Delta Node Recovery
improvements.description: Use Delta Recovery where possible to quickly reintegrate a failed node by only transferring the data that changed while it was offline.

options.label: Batch topology modifications to avoid frequent ad-hoc shifts

risks.reason: Repetitive, uncoordinated node additions and removals keep the cluster in a constant state of resource-intensive rebalancing.

improvements.title: Consolidate cluster adjustments
improvements.description: Batch node scaling activities together and map topology modifications to structured capacity expansion milestones.

options.label: Monitor ongoing background operations via the Tasks API

risks.reason: Lack of insight into live data movement or index building progress makes operational planning unpredictable.

improvements.title: Incorporate Tasks API validation
improvements.description: Use Couchbase internal REST task monitoring to verify the real-time status of rebalances, index builds, and bucket warmups.

questions.title: How do you automate Couchbase deployments and configuration management?
questions.description: Treat infrastructure as code to reduce manual toil and ensure consistency across database environments.

options.label: Define Couchbase infrastructure using Configuration Management or IaC

risks.reason: Manually deploying clusters or modifying bucket settings through the UI leads to configuration drift and irreproducible environments.

improvements.title: Implement Infrastructure as Code
improvements.description: Use Terraform, Ansible, or similar tooling to define cluster topologies, bucket quotas, and RBAC roles programmatically.

options.label: Deploy the Couchbase Autonomous Operator for Kubernetes orchestrations

risks.reason: Managing stateful database workloads manually on Kubernetes is highly error-prone and defeats the platform's orchestration benefits.

improvements.title: Adopt Operator-driven orchestration
improvements.description: Use the Couchbase Autonomous Operator to handle complex lifecycle management, auto-scaling, and self-healing natively within Kubernetes.

options.label: Automate index creation and schema updates through CI/CD pipelines

risks.reason: Manually applying index definitions in production bypasses peer review and can lock up query services if applied incorrectly.

improvements.title: Integrate database changes into pipelines
improvements.description: Store SQL++ index definitions in version control and apply them through automated deployment pipelines to ensure consistency.

options.label: Implement version control for all database configuration parameters

risks.reason: Without version control, rolling back an erroneous cluster setting or identifying who made a change during an incident is nearly impossible.

improvements.title: Version control operational settings
improvements.description: Maintain a source-of-truth repository for all cluster tuning parameters, memory quotas, and cross-datacenter replication (XDCR) setups.

questions.title: How do you respond to operational events and database incidents?
questions.description: Establish standardized procedures to investigate and resolve issues quickly while minimizing human error.

options.label: Maintain detailed runbooks for standard cluster activities

risks.reason: Ambiguity during high-pressure incidents increases human errors, such as forcing incorrect hard failovers instead of graceful ones.

improvements.title: Document precise step-by-step procedures
improvements.description: Author strict operating procedures covering graceful vs hard failovers, node swap expansions, and emergency cluster restores.

options.label: Develop incident playbooks for investigating performance degradation

risks.reason: Without standardized playbooks, different administrators will troubleshoot the same issue differently, delaying root-cause identification.

improvements.title: Standardize investigation workflows
improvements.description: Create diagnostic playbooks for common scenarios like high CPU on indexers, query timeout spikes, or XDCR replication lag.

options.label: Conduct blameless post-incident analyses after critical outages

risks.reason: Failing to conduct a structured post-incident review guarantees that systemic issues will remain unaddressed and repeat themselves.

improvements.title: Learn from all operational events
improvements.description: Define a standardized, blame-free process to document issues, identify root causes, and share lessons learned across the database team.

options.label: Conduct routine cluster failure simulation tests

risks.reason: Hidden cluster structural dependencies or application retry logic flaws remain unnoticed until a genuine production crash.

improvements.title: Incorporate chaos testing practices
improvements.description: Regularly run deliberate infrastructure failure drills to test node recovery behaviors and ensure client failover routes perform transparently.

questions.title: How do you manage software lifecycles and safely upgrade your Couchbase environment?
questions.description: Upgrade ecosystem nodes safely while minimizing software regressions and availability interruptions.

options.label: Utilize online rolling upgrade paths

risks.reason: Offline or mass node restart upgrade strategies break application availability guarantees unnecessarily.

improvements.title: Implement standard rolling upgrades
improvements.description: Leverage Couchbase cluster redundancy to perform single-node swap updates or rolling rebalances to keep data fully online during software maintenance.

options.label: Cross-reference and validate the Couchbase SDK Compatibility Matrix

risks.reason: Mismatches between older client application SDK versions and upgraded server protocols can cause connection drops or query failures.

improvements.title: Verify application client compatibility rules
improvements.description: Check application SDK support levels against the target Couchbase Server version prior to initiating infrastructure deployments.

options.label: Replicate load and traffic behaviors in staging environments prior to upgrades

risks.reason: Changes in query optimizer execution behaviors or engine regressions can cripple production performance post-upgrade if untested.

improvements.title: Run production-mimic testing suites
improvements.description: Validate target engine versions against realistic production application datasets and query workflows inside an isolated staging sandbox.

options.label: Execute post-upgrade behavioral health checks

risks.reason: Subtle query syntax warnings or service index anomalies can slip through unnoticed without targeted validation checks immediately after an upgrade.

improvements.title: Standardize system validation routines
improvements.description: Verify index structural health, cluster balance, data consistency states, and app latency metrics immediately after upgrade cycles.

questions.title: How do you continually evaluate and improve your Couchbase operations?
questions.description: Establish continuous feedback loops to optimize processes, improve efficiency, and reduce operational toil over time.

options.label: Schedule regular audits of unused indexes and obsolete buckets

risks.reason: Accumulating legacy data structures and redundant indexes slowly degrades cluster efficiency and increases backup storage footprints.

improvements.title: Implement operational cleanup routines
improvements.description: Periodically review query catalogs and system metrics to identify and drop unused secondary indexes or deprecated development buckets.

options.label: Establish a continuous feedback loop between DBAs and application developers

risks.reason: Operating the database in a silo prevents operations teams from understanding upcoming application schema changes or shifting query access patterns.

improvements.title: Align operations with development roadmaps
improvements.description: Conduct regular technical reviews with developers to align index design, query optimization, and cluster capacity with upcoming application features.

options.label: Track and review key operational metrics (e.g., MTTR, failed queries) over time

risks.reason: Without tracking historical operational data, it is impossible to know if process changes are successfully reducing downtime or improving query latencies.

improvements.title: Perform operations metrics reviews
improvements.description: Hold recurring reviews of historical metrics to identify long-term trends, prioritize technical debt reduction, and validate previous improvements.

options.label: Conduct periodic reviews of resource utilization to right-size clusters

risks.reason: Assuming a static capacity model prevents the organization from optimizing costs or scaling ahead of predictable traffic growth.

improvements.title: Iteratively assess cluster sizing
improvements.description: Routinely analyze CPU, memory, and IOPS consumption against baseline expectations to safely downscale over-provisioned nodes or scale up bottlenecks.

name: Security (SEC)
description: Protect access controls, data structures, and key material across Couchbase deployments.

questions.title: How do you manage identities and permissions for people and machines accessing Couchbase?
questions.description: Centralize identity management and enforce the principle of least privilege across all database interactions.

options.label: Integrate a Centralized Identity Provider (LDAP, SAML, PAM)

risks.reason: Without a centralized identity provider, administrators must manage scattered local accounts, increasing the risk of orphaned accounts and unauthorized access.

improvements.title: Centralize Authentication
improvements.description: Configure Couchbase to integrate with LDAP, SAML, or PAM to manage workforce user access centrally.

options.label: Enforce least-privilege via Scope and Collection-level RBAC

risks.reason: Granting full cluster or bucket-level access by default increases the blast radius if an application credential or administrator account is compromised.

improvements.title: Implement granular RBAC
improvements.description: Restrict client and administrator credentials specifically to the required Scopes or Collections rather than granting global access.

options.label: Automate platform secret and credential rotations regularly

risks.reason: Static, long-term database passwords significantly increase systemic risk exposure over extended operational time horizons.

improvements.title: Automate secrets rotation
improvements.description: Integrate Couchbase authentication with external vault tools to ensure regular, automated rotation of application passwords.

questions.title: How do you detect and investigate security events in your Couchbase environment?
questions.description: Capture and analyze events from logs to gain visibility and take action on potential threats.

options.label: Enable native Couchbase Auditing for tracking access modifications

risks.reason: Without audit logging, unauthorized changes to bucket settings, security topologies, or user permissions cannot be reliably traced for forensic investigation.

improvements.title: Enable cluster audit logging
improvements.description: Turn on the Couchbase auditing service to capture security-relevant actions and administrative changes.

options.label: Forward audit and system logs to a central SIEM or observability platform

risks.reason: Fragmented logs stored only on isolated cluster nodes slow down incident response and risk being lost completely if a node fails.

improvements.title: Centralize log management
improvements.description: Configure log forwarding (e.g., via Fluent Bit) to ship Couchbase logs to a secure, centralized SIEM for threat detection and correlation.

questions.title: How do you protect your Couchbase network resources?
questions.description: Apply multiple layers of defense to protect from external and internal network-based threats.

options.label: Restrict networking paths using explicit IP Access Lists and Security Groups

risks.reason: Exposing data interfaces or the administrative console to open network boundaries makes the cluster vulnerable to brute-force and zero-day exploits.

improvements.title: Isolate network access
improvements.description: Restrict ingress traffic strictly to known application tiers and administration bastions using Security Groups and IP Access Lists.

options.label: Incorporate private connectivity extensions (e.g., VPC Peering or PrivateLink)

risks.reason: Routing operational database connections across public transit networks introduces interception vulnerabilities and unpredictable latency.

improvements.title: Establish private backend links
improvements.description: Route data traffic inside dedicated, isolated cloud paths using AWS PrivateLink, Azure Private Link, or explicit VPC/VNet peering tunnels.

questions.title: How do you protect Couchbase data in transit and at rest?
questions.description: Protect data integrity and confidentiality through end-to-end encryption mechanisms.

options.label: Enforce strict Client-to-Cluster and Node-to-Node TLS encryption

risks.reason: Unencrypted inter-node replication traffic or client queries are highly vulnerable to credential sniffing and man-in-the-middle attacks.

improvements.title: Mandate universal transport encryption
improvements.description: Enforce strict TLS requirements (e.g., TLS 1.2+) for all client connections and enable node-to-node encryption for internal cluster traffic.

options.label: Deploy Cloud/Storage Encryption at Rest (e.g., CMEK)

risks.reason: Unencrypted physical storage volumes risk massive data leaks if the underlying disk snapshots or file systems are compromised.

improvements.title: Enable volume-level encryption
improvements.description: Enforce persistent volume block encryption or utilize Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) for all data nodes.

options.label: Implement Client-Side Field-Level Encryption (FLE) for highly sensitive PII

risks.reason: Storing raw, cleartext sensitive identifiers (like SSNs or API keys) in the database exposes confidential data to broad administrator views.

improvements.title: Incorporate SDK Field-Level Encryption
improvements.description: Leverage native Couchbase SDK FLE packages to securely encrypt highly sensitive fields before the documents leave the application memory boundaries.

questions.title: How do you prepare for and respond to security incidents involving Couchbase?
questions.description: Preparation is critical to timely investigation and recovery from security incidents.

options.label: Encrypt cluster backup archives and store them in isolated, immutable vaults

risks.reason: Unencrypted or accessible backup archives present an easy target for attackers or ransomware seeking to bypass active network controls.

improvements.title: Isolate and encrypt backups
improvements.description: Utilize built-in encryption flags in cbbackupmgr and store backups in logically air-gapped, immutable object storage.

options.label: Establish and test emergency access processes (Break-Glass Roles)

risks.reason: Relying entirely on a centralized identity provider without a tested emergency backup can completely lock administrators out of the cluster during an IdP outage.

improvements.title: Create emergency access runbooks
improvements.description: Pre-create and securely store emergency access credentials that bypass standard IdP mechanisms, strictly for use in verifiable emergency scenarios.

name: Reliability (REL)
description: Design for resilient node, availability zone, and regional failure recovery scenarios, ensuring workloads perform their intended functions correctly and consistently.

questions.title: How do you architect for server node and Availability Zone failures?
questions.description: Incorporate platform fault isolation and structure high availability cluster limits.

options.label: Configure appropriate bucket replica counts matching service criticality

risks.reason: Running zero bucket replica configurations means a single server node crash will trigger immediate unrecoverable data unavailability.

improvements.title: Define standard bucket replication counts
improvements.description: Ensure core production buckets maintain 1 to 3 replica allocations depending on target infrastructure failure tolerances.

options.label: Distribute operational nodes across physical failure zones using Server Groups

risks.reason: Failing to map rack/zone structures leaves primary documents and their corresponding replicas vulnerable to co-location on the same underlying rack or AZ.

improvements.title: Activate Couchbase Server Groups integration
improvements.description: Map infrastructure availability zones directly to explicit Couchbase Server Groups to guarantee physical isolation between primary and replica payloads.

options.label: Calibrate automatic failover timeouts against workload tolerances

risks.reason: Setting excessive auto-failover timeouts prolongs client timeouts during outages, while overly aggressive thresholds risk false failovers during minor network blips.

improvements.title: Fine-tune automatic failover settings
improvements.description: Balance cluster auto-failover parameters to handle network blips smoothly while responding quickly to true server drops.

questions.title: How do client applications manage transient cluster disruptions?
questions.description: Handle short-lived connectivity drops safely at the application layer using native SDK retry capabilities.

options.label: Deploy explicit Couchbase SDK retry strategies (e.g., BestEffortRetryStrategy)

risks.reason: Using default or poorly configured client retries causes application errors during brief cluster topology shifts or rebalances.

improvements.title: Integrate intelligent client retry structures
improvements.description: Configure client SDK retry rules to automatically queue and retry transient exceptions during topology changes.

options.label: Incorporate SDK replica read methods for read-heavy workloads

risks.reason: Read requests targeting documents on a failed active node stall completely until the cluster finishes its failover process.

improvements.title: Integrate replica read queries via the SDK
improvements.description: Incorporate client methods like getAnyReplica or getAllReplicas to fetch documents from replica copies when primary nodes are unresponsive.

options.label: Design transactional application paths around idempotent operations

risks.reason: Retrying non-idempotent mutations blind can duplicate business actions or corrupt document states.

improvements.title: Establish clear operation tracking keys
improvements.description: Ensure write operations use explicit document keys and logic that can be safely retried without unintended side effects.

questions.title: How do you manage disaster recovery across different datacenters?
questions.description: Configure, monitor, and test multi-cluster global recovery patterns.

options.label: Deploy Cross-Cluster Replication (XDCR) and define conflict resolution rules

risks.reason: Without live data replication across distinct regions, a major site outage risks catastrophic data loss and prolonged downtime.

improvements.title: Establish an active XDCR replication design
improvements.description: Configure XDCR mappings between distinct geographic clusters, matching conflict resolution choices (Revision ID vs Timestamp) to business rules.

options.label: Align cluster configurations with explicit RPO and RTO metrics

risks.reason: Vague business recovery targets lead to architectures that cannot meet data retention or uptime needs during a crisis.

improvements.title: Formalize operational recovery targets
improvements.description: Document strict RPO and RTO parameters, auditing backup schedules and XDCR bandwidth metrics against those targets.

options.label: Execute routine global data cutover and DR drills

risks.reason: An unexercised DR plan often falls short during an actual emergency due to outdated client configurations or DNS issues.

improvements.title: Conduct live data failover rehearsals
improvements.description: Run controlled DR switchover exercises to validate target application redirection, client routing, and data consistency under load.

questions.title: How do you back up data and ensure its recoverability?
questions.description: Establish persistent data protection mechanisms and validate restoration workflows to recover from catastrophic loss.

options.label: Automate routine backups using cbbackupmgr or the Backup Service

risks.reason: Failing to automate backups leaves the cluster vulnerable to accidental data deletion or volume corruption.

improvements.title: Implement automated backup schedules
improvements.description: Use the Couchbase Backup Service or scheduled cbbackupmgr tasks to periodically back up cluster data to durable storage.

options.label: Utilize Persistent Volumes for production deployments

risks.reason: Running production clusters on entirely ephemeral storage without persistent volumes prevents warm recovery and risks total data loss on node restarts.

improvements.title: Back stateful nodes with persistent volumes
improvements.description: Ensure the Data, Index, and Analytics services are deployed using persistent storage volumes to preserve data across pod or node failures.

questions.title: How do you monitor your Couchbase cluster to detect and respond to failures?
questions.description: Establish comprehensive observability to detect node stability issues, resource exhaustion, and critical platform events.

options.label: Integrate standard Prometheus metrics and node stability monitoring

risks.reason: No visibility on resident ratios or core service metrics can lead to silent degradation and heavy disk thrashing.

improvements.title: Centralize Couchbase telemetry
improvements.description: Integrate standard Couchbase Prometheus metric endpoints to continuously track node stability and resource utilization.

options.label: Monitor background operations via the Tasks API

risks.reason: Lack of insight into live data movement or index building progress makes operational planning unpredictable.

improvements.title: Incorporate Tasks API validation
improvements.description: Use Couchbase internal REST task monitoring to verify the real-time status of rebalances, index builds, and bucket warmups.

questions.title: How do you manage cluster capacity to prevent resource-induced outages?
questions.description: Ensure the cluster has sufficient memory, CPU, and disk headroom to handle peak loads and automated failover events.

options.label: Implement Couchbase Cluster Auto-scaling policies

risks.reason: Static clusters may run out of memory or CPU during unexpected traffic spikes, causing out-of-memory errors or latency timeouts.

improvements.title: Enable dynamic auto-scaling
improvements.description: Configure Couchbase Cluster Auto-scaling rules to expand and shrink nodes dynamically based on CPU, memory, or query workload metrics.

options.label: Maintain sufficient failover buffer capacity

risks.reason: If the cluster operates near 100% capacity, failing over a node will overwhelm the remaining nodes, causing a cascading failure.

improvements.title: Size for failure margins
improvements.description: Provision enough underlying capacity across Server Groups so that the remaining nodes can absorb the data and traffic of a failed node without performance degradation.

questions.title: How do you perform reliable deployments and infrastructure upgrades?
questions.description: Use automated tooling and rolling upgrade paths to minimize human error and avoid downtime during platform maintenance.

options.label: Utilize the Couchbase Autonomous Operator for Kubernetes

risks.reason: Manual deployments and scaling events are prone to configuration drift and human errors during high-pressure incidents.

improvements.title: Adopt Operator-driven orchestration
improvements.description: Deploy the Couchbase Kubernetes Operator to automate complex lifecycle management, configuration synchronization, and automated cluster recovery.

options.label: Execute online rolling upgrades and avoid ad-hoc topology shifts

risks.reason: Offline node restart strategies or frequent uncoordinated topology shifts break application availability guarantees and keep the cluster in a constant state of rebalancing.

improvements.title: Standardize rolling upgrade procedures
improvements.description: Leverage Couchbase cluster redundancy to perform single-node swap updates or rolling rebalances to keep data fully online during software maintenance.

questions.title: How do you test the resiliency of your Couchbase architecture?
questions.description: Validate that the infrastructure and applications recover smoothly from injected failures and failover routines.

options.label: Conduct routine cluster failure simulation tests

risks.reason: Hidden cluster structural dependencies or cross-zone network routing breaks remain unnoticed until a production crash.

improvements.title: Incorporate automated chaos testing practices
improvements.description: Regularly run deliberate infrastructure failure drills to test node recovery behaviors and ensure client failover routes perform transparently.

name: Performance Efficiency (PERF)
description: Optimize SQL++ execution strategies, access models, and platform resource footprints for predictable sub-millisecond responses.

questions.title: How do you optimize SQL++ (N1QL) query execution metrics?
questions.description: Minimize query scan overhead and CPU processing spikes through efficient indexing and optimized query structures.

options.label: Ensure common high-frequency queries are index-covered

risks.reason: Queries that are not index-covered require expensive data service fetches, causing high latency and memory thrashing.

improvements.title: Design comprehensive index covering strategies
improvements.description: Build Global Secondary Indexes (GSI) that include both query predicate keys and projection fields to keep executions entirely in the index tier.

options.label: Structure sargable query predicates to enable effective index pushdowns

risks.reason: Using non-sargable predicates (like wrapping index keys in functions) forces full primary index scans, causing massive CPU spikes.

improvements.title: Refactor unindexed query predicates
improvements.description: Avoid wrapping indexed attributes in runtime functions like LOWER() within the WHERE clause, ensuring the query engine can utilize index bounds efficiently.

options.label: Leverage Search (FTS) and Flex Indexes for multi-attribute ad-hoc searching

risks.reason: Forcing complex, multi-attribute ad-hoc text filters into standard GSI structures leads to bloated indexes and poor query performance.

improvements.title: Integrate Flex Index patterns with Search
improvements.description: Deploy the Couchbase Search service for text-heavy queries and enable Flex Indexing so the query service can route requests to FTS indexes automatically.

options.label: Enforce prepared statements for high-throughput parameterized executions

risks.reason: Re-parsing and planning identical query strings repeatedly adds avoidable query engine overhead, severely hurting throughput.

improvements.title: Enforce client query optimization controls
improvements.description: Leverage parameterized queries via your SDK, allowing Couchbase to cache optimal execution plans automatically.

questions.title: How are client data access paths and document models structured?
questions.description: Align storage models and data access strategies with the native strengths of the Couchbase Key-Value architecture.

options.label: Prioritize direct Key-Value (KV) access paths over SQL++ for point modifications

risks.reason: Using SQL++ queries for simple single-document lookups adds unnecessary query parsing and index lookups, bypassing the high-speed in-memory KV engine.

improvements.title: Route single-document lookups to the KV service
improvements.description: Refactor application logic to retrieve documents directly by their unique key ID using standard SDK get and upsert operations.

options.label: Model JSON documents based on access patterns and utilize Sub-Document operations

risks.reason: Poor data modeling (such as massive, unbounded arrays) forces huge network transfers and high disk I/O for minor field updates.

improvements.title: Optimize document structures for Couchbase
improvements.description: Design clean document models with reasonable bounds, and leverage SDK Sub-Document operations to read or mutate specific fields without transferring the entire document payload.

options.label: Deploy Couchbase Eventing instead of continuous client application polling

risks.reason: Frequent database polling from worker apps generates constant query load, increasing database network traffic and response latency.

improvements.title: Incorporate real-time server-side Eventing functions
improvements.description: Use the native Couchbase Eventing service to trigger lightweight, server-side JavaScript logic immediately when data changes occur.

questions.title: How do you size and scale your service infrastructure?
questions.description: Right-size cluster instances, index engines, and memory configurations using Multi-Dimensional Scaling (MDS).

options.label: Isolate engine roles (Data, Query, Index, Search) using Multi-Dimensional Scaling (MDS)

risks.reason: Colocating resource-intensive services like Query and Data on the same server nodes causes resource contention, leading to erratic KV latencies.

improvements.title: Implement Multi-Dimensional Scaling
improvements.description: Isolate different Couchbase services onto dedicated node pools, matching underlying instance types to the unique CPU, RAM, or storage needs of each specific service.

options.label: Size index allocations properly and select the appropriate index engine (Plasma)

risks.reason: Under-provisioning index memory pools causes index thrashing, driving high disk reads and severely slowing down query performance.

improvements.title: Optimize index engine selection and sizing
improvements.description: Size index RAM quotas to maintain healthy resident ratios, and leverage the Plasma engine to ensure memory-optimized index traversals.

options.label: Evaluate the Magma Storage Engine for high-density, disk-heavy datasets

risks.reason: Using memory-heavy storage backends for massive datasets can become cost-prohibitive due to the high RAM footprint required just to maintain document keys.

improvements.title: Deploy Magma for high-volume storage
improvements.description: Configure large buckets to use the Magma storage engine, enabling sub-millisecond operations even when only a small fraction of data fits in RAM.

questions.title: How do you maintain optimal query execution plans and database statistics?
questions.description: Ensure the query engine has the necessary statistical data and advice to formulate the most efficient execution paths.

options.label: Utilize the Cost-Based Optimizer (CBO) and regularly UPDATE STATISTICS

risks.reason: Without updated collection statistics, the query engine relies on rule-based heuristics that can pick suboptimal index paths for complex joins.

improvements.title: Automate Cost-Based Optimizer statistics gathering
improvements.description: Run the UPDATE STATISTICS statement regularly on active collections to feed the Cost-Based Optimizer accurate data distribution metrics.

options.label: Periodically consult the Couchbase Index Advisor

risks.reason: Relying purely on manual query tuning often misses subtle opportunities for index consolidation or optimization.

improvements.title: Leverage the ADVISE function
improvements.description: Use the Index Advisor (via the ADVISE statement) to automatically analyze slow SQL++ queries and generate optimal CREATE INDEX recommendations.

options.label: Enable and monitor completed requests logging for slow queries

risks.reason: Unindexed or unoptimized SQL++ queries run undetected, consuming shared cluster CPU resources and starving legitimate traffic.

improvements.title: Capture and analyze slow SQL++ queries
improvements.description: Leverage the system:completed_requests catalog or log thresholds to actively audit and optimize slow query executions.

questions.title: How do your client applications efficiently interact with the database cluster?
questions.description: Utilize SDK best practices to maximize network throughput and minimize connection overhead.

options.label: Implement explicit Bulk Operations for large dataset modifications

risks.reason: Executing thousands of individual write requests sequentially adds massive network round-trip overhead and throttles overall data ingestion rates.

improvements.title: Adopt asynchronous or reactive bulk batching
improvements.description: Refactor data ingestion pipelines to utilize native Couchbase SDK Bulk Operations, maximizing network pipelining and throughput.

options.label: Defer index builds during massive data imports

risks.reason: Creating indexes individually during heavy data loads causes the indexer to repeatedly scan the data service, slowing down write performance.

improvements.title: Utilize the DEFER BUILD clause
improvements.description: Use the 'WITH {"defer_build": true}' option when defining multiple secondary indexes, and use BUILD INDEX to construct them efficiently in a single pass.

options.label: Enable SDK Response Time Observability to profile slow operations

risks.reason: Without application-side tracing, it is difficult to determine if latency is caused by network routing, SDK serialization, or the database engine.

improvements.title: Trace end-to-end SDK performance
improvements.description: Enable Response Time Observability within the Couchbase SDK to emit threshold-based logging and distributed trace spans for slow operations.

questions.title: How do you optimize Full Text Search (FTS) and Analytics workloads?
questions.description: Isolate heavy analytical and text-search workloads to prevent them from impacting operational data latencies.

options.label: Route ad-hoc analytical and complex aggregate queries to the Analytics Service

risks.reason: Executing massive, cluster-wide aggregations or ad-hoc data explorations on the operational Query Service can exhaust CPU resources and degrade application latency.

improvements.title: Isolate analytical queries
improvements.description: Deploy the Couchbase Enterprise Analytics Service to handle complex, long-running, and ad-hoc data explorations without impacting operational KV or Query nodes.

options.label: Utilize Index Partitioning for massive Full Text Search (FTS) indexes

risks.reason: A single massive FTS index can hit physical node resource constraints, leading to slow text scoring and high memory consumption during mutations.

improvements.title: Distribute FTS indexes across nodes
improvements.description: Configure Index Partitioning for large FTS indexes, distributing the query scattering and gathering phases across multiple search nodes to increase throughput.

options.label: Restrict FTS Index scope using specific Type Mappings and Custom Analyzers

risks.reason: Using the default dynamic mapping for FTS indexes every single field in every document, creating enormous, slow indexes filled with irrelevant data.

improvements.title: Target specific fields for FTS
improvements.description: Disable dynamic mapping and explicitly define Type Mappings and Child Fields to index only the exact text attributes required by the application.

name: Cost Optimization (COST)
description: Run Couchbase systems to deliver business value at the lowest price point by right-sizing infrastructure, managing data lifecycles, and tracking resource attribution.

questions.title: How do you govern and monitor your Couchbase resource usage and costs?
questions.description: Establish policies and procedures to monitor, appropriately allocate, and alert on costs associated with your database workloads.

options.label: Identify cost attribution using comprehensive resource tagging

risks.reason: Without tagging underlying instances or Kubernetes pods, organizations cannot track resources over their lifetime, making it impossible to attribute database costs to specific business units or applications.

improvements.title: Implement a tagging scheme
improvements.description: Gather stakeholders to define a tagging schema for all underlying Couchbase infrastructure to enable cost allocation and chargebacks.

options.label: Configure billing alerts and anomaly detection

risks.reason: Failing to set budget limits and anomaly detection can result in severe 'cost shocks' if a cluster unexpectedly scales or network traffic spikes.

improvements.title: Create daily cost and usage budgets
improvements.description: Configure cloud budget alerts and cost anomaly detection to notify teams immediately when database operational costs exceed predefined thresholds.

questions.title: How do you optimize Couchbase compute and infrastructure costs?
questions.description: Select the appropriate resource type, size, and pricing models to meet workload performance needs at the lowest cost.

options.label: Utilize Multi-Dimensional Scaling (MDS) to isolate services

risks.reason: Scaling all nodes identically forces you to over-provision expensive compute or memory resources globally, even if only one specific service (like Indexing) is constrained.

improvements.title: Leverage target service auto-scaling
improvements.description: Utilize Couchbase Multi-Dimensional Scaling (MDS) properties to scale only the specific service layers (Data, Query, Index) that are resource-constrained.

options.label: Implement Couchbase Cluster Auto-scaling based on demand

risks.reason: Provisioning static clusters for peak capacity means paying for idle computing resources during periods of low application demand.

improvements.title: Enable dynamic auto-scaling
improvements.description: Configure Couchbase Cluster Auto-scaling rules to expand and shrink nodes dynamically based on CPU, memory, or query workload metrics.

options.label: Adopt cost-effective pricing models (e.g., Reserved Instances / Savings Plans)

risks.reason: Running predictable, steady-state database clusters entirely on On-Demand instances misses out on significant volume discount savings.

improvements.title: Review and implement commitment pricing
improvements.description: Analyze steady-state database node usage and apply Reserved Instances (RIs) or Savings Plans to reduce the hourly compute cost of the baseline workload.

questions.title: How do you optimize Couchbase data storage costs?
questions.description: Manage data lifecycles, limit index overhead, and align storage models to reduce unnecessary block storage expenses.

options.label: Apply native Time-To-Live (TTL) settings for transient data

risks.reason: Allowing short-lived session or cache data to accumulate indefinitely inflates storage footprints and drives up cluster scaling costs.

improvements.title: Enforce automated TTL retention rules
improvements.description: Configure document or collection-level TTL settings to automatically purge old or temporary documents without application overhead.

options.label: Utilize Ephemeral Buckets for pure cache layers

risks.reason: Using standard persistent buckets for transient caching workloads incurs unneeded disk write overhead and increases underlying block storage costs.

improvements.title: Evaluate Ephemeral bucket configurations
improvements.description: Deploy Couchbase Ephemeral Buckets for pure caching layers to keep operations entirely in-memory and remove persistent block storage requirements.

options.label: Identify and remove redundant or duplicate indexes

risks.reason: Unused or redundant indexes waste expensive memory quota and disk space while simultaneously slowing down mutation write performance.

improvements.title: Establish index cleanup routines
improvements.description: Regularly audit index usage statistics via system catalogs, removing indexes that do not support active query workflows.

questions.title: How do you manage data transfer and network costs?
questions.description: Plan and monitor data transfer charges to make architectural decisions that minimize operational networking expenses.

options.label: Use VPC Endpoints or PrivateLink for internal traffic

risks.reason: Routing internal database traffic or backups through public NAT gateways incurs high outbound internet data transfer processing charges.

improvements.title: Implement private network routing
improvements.description: Use VPC Endpoints or PrivateLink to keep application-to-database communication on the private provider network, reducing per-GB data transfer costs.

options.label: Optimize Cross-Cluster Replication (XDCR) regional traffic

risks.reason: Replicating entire buckets across geographic cloud regions without filtering can lead to unexpectedly high inter-region bandwidth bills.

improvements.title: Monitor and filter XDCR transfers
improvements.description: Analyze cross-region replication needs and implement XDCR filtering so that only strictly necessary business data is transmitted across regional boundaries.

questions.title: How do you manage the lifecycle of your Couchbase environments to prevent waste?
questions.description: Implement resource management from inception to end-of-life, shutting down unused resources to reduce waste.

options.label: Hibernate or pause non-production clusters during off-hours

risks.reason: Leaving development and testing database environments running 24/7 wastes approximately 70% of potential operational cost savings.

improvements.title: Implement Couchbase Cluster Hibernation
improvements.description: Utilize Couchbase Cluster Hibernation or automated infrastructure schedules to pause non-production clusters outside of core business hours.

options.label: Audit and remove sample buckets, unused data, and orphaned volumes

risks.reason: Retaining unused sample data buckets or detached physical disk volumes incurs ongoing block storage fees for zero business value.

improvements.title: Automate unused asset cleanup
improvements.description: Ensure development Sample Buckets are not deployed in higher environments, and actively monitor and delete orphaned block storage volumes.

name: Data Management & Consistency (DATA)
description: Manage consistency controls, write durability guarantees, and logical organization shapes across evolving Couchbase datasets.

questions.title: How do you manage write durability and concurrency controls?
questions.description: Balance application data integrity guarantees with network latency, and ensure safe concurrent document modifications.

options.label: Leverage synchronous Durability Levels for critical business writes

risks.reason: Using asynchronous writes for high-value transactional data risks silent data loss if an active node fails before changes are replicated.

improvements.title: Enforce explicit SDK Durability Levels
improvements.description: Configure critical mutations to use explicit synchronous durability levels like Majority or MajorityAndPersistToActive to guarantee replication before acknowledgment.

options.label: Enforce Check-And-Set (CAS) tokens for optimistic concurrency control

risks.reason: Without concurrency controls, concurrent application threads can overwrite each other's updates, leading to data corruption.

improvements.title: Incorporate CAS mutation flows
improvements.description: Utilize native Couchbase CAS tokens inside application write and update logic to protect concurrent mutations from stepping on each other.

options.label: Utilize explicit document locking (getAndLock) for pessimistic concurrency

risks.reason: Relying purely on optimistic concurrency for highly contested single documents can lead to excessive application retry loops and CPU overhead.

improvements.title: Implement pessimistic locking for hot documents
improvements.description: Use the SDK's getAndLock operation to temporarily lock highly contested documents during complex read-modify-write cycles.

questions.title: How do you structure data lifecycles and logical isolation?
questions.description: Control database volume growth and manage document schema transformations over time using multi-tenant boundaries.

options.label: Organize datasets logically using Scopes and Collections

risks.reason: Dumping unrelated datasets into a single bucket complicates index design, safety boundaries, and data lifecycles, while creating separate buckets adds heavy cluster overhead.

improvements.title: Adopt a clean Scopes and Collections taxonomy
improvements.description: Group data structures logically into Scopes and Collections within a bucket to simplify access controls, indexing, and multi-tenant isolation.

options.label: Apply native Time-To-Live (TTL) expirations for transient data

risks.reason: Relying on manual application sweeps to delete old data leads to unbounded disk growth and degraded memory resident ratios.

improvements.title: Automate document expiration
improvements.description: Configure document or collection-level TTL settings to automatically purge old or temporary documents natively within the data service.

options.label: Implement application-tier schema versioning for evolving JSON layouts

risks.reason: Modifying document properties without backwards compatibility logic can break active SQL++ index queries or cause application crashes on older client nodes.

improvements.title: Establish explicit schema evolution patterns
improvements.description: Include a structural version field in your JSON models, handling schema updates gracefully within the application reading layer.

questions.title: How do you balance SQL++ query consistency with performance?
questions.description: Tune index scan consistency to meet business requirements without unnecessarily degrading query throughput.

options.label: Configure appropriate scan_consistency levels per query

risks.reason: Applying 'request_plus' globally forces the indexer to wait for all mutations to process before returning results, severely impacting read throughput.

improvements.title: Optimize query consistency targets
improvements.description: Evaluate query requirements and use 'not_bounded' for general analytics or 'request_plus' strictly for operations requiring immediate read-your-own-writes consistency.

options.label: Utilize Covering Indexes for high-frequency queries

risks.reason: Requiring the query service to fetch documents from the data service for every index scan adds significant latency to read operations.

improvements.title: Design comprehensive index covering strategies
improvements.description: Build Global Secondary Indexes (GSI) that include both query predicate keys and projection fields to keep executions entirely in the index tier.

options.label: Enforce prepared statements for high-throughput parameterized executions

risks.reason: Re-parsing and planning identical query strings repeatedly adds avoidable query engine CPU overhead.

improvements.title: Enforce client query optimization controls
improvements.description: Leverage parameterized queries via your SDK, allowing Couchbase to cache optimal execution plans automatically.

questions.title: How do you maintain atomicity across multiple document modifications?
questions.description: Ensure data integrity when performing complex, multi-document, or multi-collection workflows.

options.label: Implement Couchbase Distributed ACID Transactions via SDK or SQL++

risks.reason: Building custom two-phase commit logic in application code is highly error-prone and can leave orphaned records if an application node crashes mid-process.

improvements.title: Leverage native ACID transactions
improvements.description: Use the native Distributed ACID Transactions API in the Couchbase SDK or SQL++ to automatically handle rollbacks and consistency across multiple documents.

options.label: Utilize Sub-Document operations for atomic updates within a single JSON structure

risks.reason: Fetching large documents just to update a single array element consumes excessive network bandwidth and increases CAS conflict probabilities.

improvements.title: Optimize with Sub-Document API
improvements.description: Use Couchbase Sub-Document operations to atomically manipulate specific fields or arrays within a JSON document without retrieving the entire payload.

options.label: Design transactional application paths around idempotent operations

risks.reason: Retrying non-idempotent mutations blindly during transient network errors can duplicate business actions or corrupt document states.

improvements.title: Establish clear operation tracking keys
improvements.description: Ensure write operations use explicit document keys and tracking logic that can be safely retried without unintended side effects.

questions.title: How do you resolve data conflicts in active-active cross-datacenter deployments?
questions.description: Manage Cross-Cluster Replication (XDCR) to prevent divergent data sets during multi-directional syncing.

options.label: Enable Timestamp-based Conflict Resolution for replicated data

risks.reason: Relying on default Revision ID conflict resolution in an active-active setup can lead to older data overwriting newer data if mutations happen concurrently across regions.

improvements.title: Standardize XDCR conflict strategies
improvements.description: Configure Timestamp-based Conflict Resolution to ensure the most recent mutation always wins globally.

options.label: Implement XDCR Advanced Filtering

risks.reason: Replicating entire buckets across geographic networks without filtering consumes excessive bandwidth for data that might only be needed locally.

improvements.title: Filter XDCR replication traffic
improvements.description: Use XDCR Advanced Filtering with regular expressions to replicate only the specific keys or collections necessary for remote operations.

options.label: Monitor XDCR Conflict Logging

risks.reason: Failing to monitor conflict resolution logs makes it difficult to audit why specific document versions were retained or discarded across clusters.

improvements.title: Enable and review XDCR Conflict Logging
improvements.description: Enable XDCR Conflict Logging to maintain visibility into how concurrent mutations are resolved across multi-datacenter environments.

questions.title: How do you automate complex data enrichment and reactive workflows?
questions.description: Process data changes and enforce business rules reliably as mutations happen across the cluster.

options.label: Use the Couchbase Eventing Service for asynchronous data triggers

risks.reason: Relying on external application polling to detect database changes introduces latency and increases continuous read load on the cluster.

improvements.title: Adopt Event-driven architectures
improvements.description: Deploy Couchbase Eventing functions to listen for data mutations and automatically trigger enrichment, cascade deletes, or external REST API calls.

options.label: Leverage Eventing Timers for delayed execution workflows

risks.reason: Building custom application schedulers to manage delayed document state changes introduces unnecessary external dependencies.

improvements.title: Implement native execution timers
improvements.description: Use Eventing Timers to schedule business logic (like document archival or shipping notifications) at precise times in the future.

options.label: Enforce strict Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) on Eventing functions

risks.reason: Over-privileged Eventing functions could inadvertently modify or delete data outside of their intended scope or collection boundaries.

improvements.title: Scope Eventing execution privileges
improvements.description: Assign specific RBAC roles to Eventing functions to limit their read and write access strictly to the required Collections.
